trust_decision.summary: Whether a gitify:// OAuth callback belongs to the login attempt this client started; at the pinned commit the renderer's web-flow callback handler accepts any callback with a code (or error) and never sends or compares an OAuth state.

landing_point.why: performGitHubWebOAuth is the only OAuth web-flow implementation and builds the authorization URL and handles the callback in one function; 'OAuth state validation' leads straight here.

fix_sites.entry_point: Login with OAuth App route (/login/github/oauth-app, also reached via Accounts re-authenticate) -> useLogins.loginWithOAuthApp -> performGitHubWebOAuth; generation of state on the authorization URL
gitify:// protocol URL (app 'open-url' on macOS, 'second-instance' argv on Windows/Linux) -> handleProtocolURL -> AUTH_CALLBACK IPC -> handleCallback; unparseable URL now ignored instead of rejecting
same gitify:// protocol callback; new state equality check before both code and error branches
new helper src/renderer/utils/auth/state.ts generateOAuthState, called only from performGitHubWebOAuth

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Only weak levers exist: a solver could argue that error callbacks (error= without code) or unparseable gitify:// URLs are harmless and leave them able to reject the pending login, since they cannot bind a foreign account.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate callback carrying the matching state must still resolve the pending login, a matching-state error callback must still reject with the GitHub error text, and a forged/mismatched/unparseable callback must be ignored without tearing down the still-pending attempt (over-broad fix: rejecting or unsubscribing on any bad callback).

O6_input_shapes: callback with code and mismatched state
callback with code and no state
error callback with no or mismatched state

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second OAuthWebAppSupport implementation (e.g. a GitLab or Gitea/Forgejo OAuth web flow) with its own authorize URL builder and gitify:// callback handler lacking state.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The forge adapter interface already defines an optional oauthWebApp bundle and the Gitea adapter comments anticipate adding OAuth support later (src/renderer/utils/forges/gitea/adapter.ts:79); a maintainer would copy the GitHub flow into another forge package.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A main-process callback path (e.g. a loopback/redirect handler or a deep-link 'gitify://oauth' consumer in main) that completes the login without passing through the renderer's state check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The main process already owns protocol handling and forwards URLs verbatim; moving or duplicating callback parsing into main is a plausible refactor and would sit in a different package from the landing point.

O9_family: CWE-352 login CSRF / OAuth state not validated (A01)

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=24, pnpm 12.13.0, Vite+ (vp) with vitest; Electron app
O10_build.project_tests: src/renderer/utils/forges/github/flows.test.ts (vitest, happy-dom project; mocks window.gitify.onAuthCallback and openExternalLink, no GUI needed)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a state to the authorize URL and check it only in the code branch, leaving error callbacks and the unparseable-URL reject path able to abort the pending login.

out_of_scope_notes: handleProtocolURL forwards any gitify:// URL to the renderer with only a prefix check (src/main/lifecycle/startup.ts:45-50); not pursued.
Callback URLs, which may include auth codes, are logged in full (src/renderer/utils/forges/github/flows.ts:90-93); not pursued.
